## Overview

**v0.5.3 — smarter tabs and consistent logical sizing across every desktop.**
This release redesigns the tab bar around safer fixed controls, lets shells
drive tab titles through OSC 0/2, and gives terminal content and tab labels
explicit cross-platform logical sizing contracts. It also makes every new shell
start in the home directory, removes fish's 10-second startup wait on Linux and
macOS, and fixes diagnostic timing so wall-clock adjustments cannot corrupt
performance samples.

The changes were exercised on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Automated validation
also covers Linux, macOS, and Windows on both x86_64 and aarch64.

There are no config schema changes since v0.5.2. Newly generated configs now use
`font.size_point: 15` and `font.line_height_ratio: 1.1` on every platform;
existing config files keep their explicit values. **macOS still requires macOS
14 (Sonoma) or later.**

## What's new since v0.5.2

### Tabs

- **Shell-driven tab titles** ([#269](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/269))
  — OSC 0/2 titles from bash, zsh, fish, and other shells now update active and
  background tabs. A 150 ms debounce suppresses the brief command title emitted
  by short commands, new tabs wait for the shell before showing a `Tab N`
  fallback, and manually renamed tabs remain under user control.
- **Safer fixed tab controls** ([#268](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/268))
  — per-tab close buttons are gone. Navigation, close-active-tab, and new-tab
  controls now stay at the right edge in the order `[<][tabs][>][×][+]`, with
  clear per-button hover feedback and font-independent vector icons. This keeps
  tab switching away from destructive click targets.
- **More title in the same space** ([#271](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/271))
  — long titles use one U+2026 ellipsis cell, rename reserves less trailing
  space, and IME cursor placement remains stable at the truncation boundary.
- **Scale-correct spacing** ([#270](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/270))
  — tab gaps and control hover insets are logical points multiplied by the
  current display scale. Linux also follows the same control-over-title draw
  order as macOS and Windows, preventing a final glyph from bleeding into the
  navigation area.
- **Independent tab-label sizing** ([#272](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/272))
  — tab titles, rename text, preedit text, and tab icons use a dedicated 13
  logical-point font resource. Terminal `font.size_point` changes no longer
  stretch the tab bar, whose height is now a fixed 28 logical points.

### Fonts and scaling

- **One logical sizing contract** ([#273](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/273))
  — Linux, macOS, and Windows now apply `logical size x OS display scale`, then
  use the same final ceiling rule for cell metrics. Windows no longer rounds
  DirectWrite metrics before applying configured ratios, and rational display
  scales avoid floating-point boundary overshoot.
- **Common defaults for new configs** — `font.size_point` is 15 and
  `font.line_height_ratio` is 1.1 on all three platforms. Existing configs are
  not migrated. The size is deliberately logical rather than a physical
  1/72-inch or millimeter guarantee; different fonts and viewport sizes can
  still produce different apparent glyph sizes and visible row counts.

### Terminal compatibility

- **Shells start in the home directory** ([#265](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/265))
  — launcher location no longer leaks into the child shell. Linux and macOS use
  the user's home directly; Windows starts native shells in the Windows home and
  adds `--cd ~` to WSL commands unless the user already supplied `--cd`.
- **Terminal query responses on Linux and macOS** ([#266](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/266))
  — DA1/2/3, DSR, DECRQM, kitty keyboard queries, XTVERSION, color-scheme DSR,
  and OSC color queries now receive terminal responses through the PTY. fish 4
  reaches its first prompt immediately instead of waiting 10 seconds, and can
  detect the active dark/light theme.
- **Windows keeps the ConPTY-owned query path** — conhost remains responsible
  for application queries. Its headless OSC 10/11 default colors are not exposed
  to TildaZ, a limitation also observed in Windows Terminal; `COLORFGBG` remains
  the supported WSL dark/light signal.
- **Updated pinned terminal core** — libghostty-vt is pinned to a newer exact
  commit with built-in xterm and kitty color-query responses. The Windows CI
  dependency fetch was separately verified with the upstream tarball's symbolic
  link before this release.

### Reliability and diagnostics

- **Monotonic performance timing** ([#274](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/274))
  — elapsed-time samples use Zig `std.time.Instant` instead of a realtime
  calendar timestamp. System clock corrections can no longer underflow or
  inflate PTY, parser, renderer, or frame duration counters. These counters are
  diagnostic only and do not control application behavior.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Linux portable (glibc 2.28+) | `tildaz-v0.5.3-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.tar.gz` | Extract, run `./install.sh` (writes `.desktop` + icon under `~/.local/share/`, no `sudo`). |
| Linux Debian / Ubuntu | `tildaz_0.5.3_{amd64,arm64}.deb` | `sudo dpkg -i tildaz_*.deb` or open with the Software app. |
| Linux Fedora / RHEL / openSUSE | `tildaz-0.5.3-1.{x86_64,aarch64}.rpm` | `sudo dnf install ./tildaz-*.rpm` |
| Linux distro-independent | `TildaZ-0.5.3-{x86_64,aarch64}.AppImage` | `chmod +x` and run. FUSE optional. glibc 2.28+. |
| Arch / Manjaro / EndeavourOS | `tildaz-0.5.3-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst` | `sudo pacman -U tildaz-*.pkg.tar.zst` (x86_64 only). |
| macOS 14+ universal | `tildaz-v0.5.3-macos.dmg` | Apple Silicon + Intel. Drag `TildaZ.app` to Applications. Ad-hoc signed. |
| Windows 10/11 x64 | `tildaz-v0.5.3-win-x64.zip` | Unzip anywhere. `tildaz.exe` + bundled ConPTY. Unsigned. |
| Windows 11 ARM64 | `tildaz-v0.5.3-win-arm64.zip` | ARM64-native binary + ARM64 ConPTY. Unsigned. |

**A running Wayland session is required on Linux; TildaZ does not have an X11
backend.** Linux packages use the direct Wayland client and retain the same
glibc 2.28+ baseline as v0.5.2.

## Migration from v0.5.2

- **Existing configs are read unchanged.** Only newly generated configs receive
  the common 15 / 1.1 font defaults.
- Tab labels are fixed at 13 logical points and no longer follow terminal font
  size or line-height settings.
- Shells now start in the home directory. A Windows WSL command with an explicit
  `--cd` keeps the user-provided directory.
- **macOS minimum remains macOS 14 (Sonoma).** macOS 13 users should stay on
  v0.5.0.

## Known limitations

- **macOS info / error dialog keys are intermittent** ([#249](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/249))
  — an NSAlert can rarely ignore the first Esc / Enter because the accessory-app
  modal does not always become the key window in time.
- **Windows OSC 10/11 default-color queries** ([#266](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/266))
  — headless ConPTY does not expose its default foreground/background colors, so
  `fish_terminal_color_theme` may remain empty in WSL. `COLORFGBG` is still
  supplied from the configured TildaZ theme.
- **KDE floating dock overlap** ([#206](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/206))
  — a Plasma floating panel can be partially covered. Turning off the panel's
  Floating option avoids the compositor limitation.
- **VSCode / Electron (X11) Hangul IME** ([#194](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/194))
  — switching through some X11-fronted editor sessions can leave the fcitx5
  Wayland frontend inactive until another native Wayland app receives focus.
- The Linux `wl_shm` renderer remains a software path.
